reason: This passage (Exodus 3) depicts Moses' divine calling and commissioning at the burning bush, not a leader dealing with ungrateful people. While Moses is the central human figure and the narrative includes his perspective, the story focuses on God's revelation to Moses of his identity and mission to liberate the Israelites from Egypt. The text describes God hearing the cry of the oppressed Israelites and commissioning Moses—it does not show Moses as an established leader managing ungrateful or complaining people. Moses hasn't yet assumed leadership of the Israelites, and there is no depiction of ungrateful people in this passage. The perspective is broader than a single leader's viewpoint, encompassing narrative description, divine speech, and Moses' responses to his calling.
